items.topic: What file paths are expected to change?
items.context: Both acceptance_allow and acceptance_deny are missing from spec.json. Defining change boundaries enables sandbox scoping and post-execution review. This depends on d1 and d2.

options.label: Broad: scenarios/<target>/**
options.rationale: Allow changes anywhere in the target scenario. Appropriate for features that touch multiple layers.

options.label: Targeted subdirectories only
options.rationale: Restrict to specific subdirectories (e.g., api/internal/backlog/**, ui/src/components/backlog/**).

options.label: Defer until scope is decided
options.rationale: Wait for d1 and d2 answers before defining acceptance boundaries.

items.notes: Pre-selected C since this depends on decisions d1 and d2.

items.context: If this item is about adding effort estimation to backlog items, there are several approaches with different tradeoffs. This decision shapes the data model and UI complexity.

options.label: Simple numeric field (story points or hours)
options.rationale: Add a single 'effort' field to spec.json. Minimal complexity, easy to sort/filter. Most teams use Fibonacci-like scales (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13).

options.label: T-shirt sizing (XS, S, M, L, XL)
options.rationale: Categorical effort labels. Simpler for humans to assign, but harder to aggregate or use in calculations.

options.label: Multi-dimensional (effort + complexity + risk)
options.rationale: Richer model with separate dimensions. More information but higher overhead per item.

options.label: AI-estimated with manual override
options.rationale: Use item context (description, plan, workshop answers) to auto-estimate effort, with human override. Most sophisticated but requires training data.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach.

items.context: Once effort data exists, it needs to surface somewhere useful. This affects which UI components and API endpoints need changes.

options.label: Backlog list view only
options.rationale: Show effort on workshop-item-card in the backlog page. Minimal UI change.

options.label: Backlog list + detail page + initiative rollups
options.rationale: Full integration: list badges, detail panel section, and aggregated effort per initiative.

options.label: API only (no UI yet)
options.rationale: Add to data model and API first, defer UI to a follow-up item.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify where effort should appear.

items.text: The current spec.json schema includes priority (1-10), status, tags, depends_on, initiative, acceptance_allow, and acceptance_deny fields — but no effort or complexity field. Adding effort would be a new field addition to the schema.

The swarm-manager UI already has backlog list/detail views with badges for readiness, dependencies, initiatives, and agent status. An effort badge would follow the same pattern (see workshop-item-card.tsx and the existing badge components).
